title: API key shipped in client-side JavaScript; README says it never leaves the server
evidence: api.js is loaded by index.html:25 as a plain <script>. The key is sent as a Bearer header at api.js:6 and api.js:11 from the browser. README.md:6 states 'the API key never leaves the server'. Traced.
failing_case: Open the page, View Source or DevTools > Network on any request: the Authorization header and the api.js source both show the key. Anyone with it can call POST /refunds directly.
remediation: Move the key to a server-side proxy that authenticates the user and enforces refund limits; rotate the shipped key; correct the README.

title: Customer name, id and status interpolated into innerHTML unescaped
evidence: app.js:32 builds the row with template literals and assigns via tb.innerHTML +=. o.customer.name goes into text context, o.id into an attribute (data-id="..."), o.status into a class attribute. No escaping anywhere. Traced.
failing_case: A customer registers with the name . Every operator who opens the dashboard runs it, in a page that also holds the API key (api.js:3). Name `">
remediation: Build rows with createElement and textContent / dataset, or escape every interpolated value; allow-list o.status against paid|refunded|pending before using it as a class.

title: Selection list only ever grows: unchecking does nothing, duplicates and hidden pages stay selected
evidence: app.js:35 pushes on check and has no branch for uncheck. renderTable re-creates all checkboxes unchecked on every page change, filter change and keystroke, but `selected` (app.js:5) is never reset, and is never cleared after refund (app.js:49-52). The handler is also re-bound after each render so state and UI diverge. Traced.
failing_case: Tick order A, untick A, tick B, click Refund: selected = [A, B]; A is refunded though the user unchecked it. Or tick A on page 1, go to page 2, tick B: refund sends A and B while the UI shows only B ticked. Clicking Refund twice re-sends the same ids.
remediation: Keep selection as a Set updated on both check and uncheck, re-apply checked state after render, clear it after a confirmed refund, and show the count next to the button.

quote: - **Pricing:** the Team plan is $15 per seat; 12 seats on annual billing at 20% off is $1,440 a year.
title: Pricing arithmetic is wrong under either reading
evidence: If $15 is per seat per month: 15 x 12 seats x 12 months = $2,160; 20% off = $1,728. If $15 is per seat per year: 15 x 12 = $180; 20% off = $144. $1,440 matches neither (it is $144 x 10 or $120 x 12).
failing_case: A customer is quoted $1,440 for 12 seats; the stated terms give $1,728 (or $144), so the invoice disagrees with the published price.
remediation: State the billing period (per seat per month) and the correct total ($1,728), or whatever the real price is.

title: Stat labels and pager buttons fail contrast: #aaa on white and on cream, at 11-12 px
evidence: #aaa on #fff is about 2.3:1; #aaa on #F4F1EA (Prev/Next, styles.css:18) is about 2.1:1; the eyebrow #c7c2f0 on #6366f1 (styles.css:4) is about 2.7:1 at 11px. All are under the 4.5:1 AA minimum (WCAG 1.4.3). Computed from the hex values by hand; page not rendered.
failing_case: REVENUE / ORDERS / AVG ORDER labels and the Prev / Next buttons are hard to read for low-vision users and in sunlight.
remediation: Use #595959 or darker for .lbl and buttons (at least 4.5:1), lighten the eyebrow to #fff or darken the gradient, and raise text to 12-14px minimum.

quote: - **Fully accessible:** meets WCAG 2.1 AA, including 44 px touch targets (criterion 2.5.5).
title: README accessibility claim is contradicted by the code, and 2.5.5 is a AAA criterion
evidence: Contradicted by styles.css:19 (focus removed), styles.css:9/18 (contrast), index.html:19 (span control), index.html:17 (no labels), styles.css:18 (buttons with 2px 4px padding at 12px font, about 20px tall). 2.5.5 Target Size is AAA in WCAG 2.1, not part of AA.
failing_case: A buyer or auditor relies on the 'meets WCAG 2.1 AA' statement and ships it; it fails several AA and A criteria and the 44px targets are not present.
remediation: Remove the claim until an audit passes, or fix the listed failures; state 2.5.5 as an AAA goal if kept.

title: refund() does not await the request and always reports success
evidence: api.js:11 calls fetch without await or catch, then api.js:12 returns {ok:true} immediately. app.js:51 turns that into the toast 'Refunded N orders!'. Network failure, 401, 500 are never seen; a rejected fetch is an unhandled rejection. Traced.
failing_case: Go offline (or the server returns 500), select two orders, click Refund selected. The toast says 'Refunded 2 orders!' and no money moved.
remediation: await the fetch, check res.ok, return {ok:false, error} on failure; show the toast only on confirmed success and show the cause and a retry on failure.

title: Pagination is 1-based in the label but 0-based in the slice: first 10 orders never shown
evidence: app.js:3 starts page = 1; app.js:27 slices from page*10 = 10. Page 1 therefore shows orders 11-20. Orders 1-10 are only reachable via Prev, which goes to page 0. Traced.
failing_case: Load 25 orders. Page 1 shows orders 11-20; the 5 newest/first orders (1-10) are invisible until Prev is clicked, and then the label reads 'Page 0'.
remediation: Use (page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE, or make page 0-based and display page + 1.

title: Order status is conveyed by a coloured dot only; row checkboxes have no name
evidence: The dot has no text, title or aria-label; paid/refunded/pending differ only by #3c3, #c33, #cc3 (green and red are indistinguishable for common colour-blindness; #cc3 on white is under 3:1). The checkbox in the same row has no label, so a screen reader hears 'checkbox' for each. WCAG 1.4.1 (A), 4.1.2 (A), 1.4.11 (AA). Traced.
failing_case: A screen-reader user or a deuteranope cannot tell a refunded order from a paid one, the exact thing the refund task depends on.
remediation: Print the status as text (e.g. 'Refunded') next to or instead of the dot, and give each checkbox aria-label="Select order <id> for <customer>".

title: Request per keystroke with no debounce, no cancel, and responses applied in arrival order; no error handling
evidence: load() (app.js:38-43) awaits getOrders and assigns `orders` whatever finished last. No AbortController, no sequence check, no try/catch; a rejected fetch or a non-array error body (api.js:7 returns res.json() with no res.ok check) leaves the UI stale or makes orders.slice throw at app.js:28. Traced.
failing_case: Type 'ann' quickly: requests for 'a', 'an', 'ann' go out. If the 'a' response arrives last, the table and stats show results for 'a' under a search box that says 'ann'. On a 500 with a JSON error object, orders becomes an object and the table render throws.
remediation: Debounce input, abort the previous request (or ignore responses whose sequence number is stale), check res.ok in getOrders, and show a loading and error state.

title: Refund fires on one click with no confirmation; README claims refunds are confirmed
evidence: No confirm(), dialog or undo anywhere in app.js or index.html. README.md:9 says 'Refunds are confirmed before they are sent.' Traced.
failing_case: Select 40 orders and misclick the purple Refund selected control: the refund request is sent immediately. With nothing selected it also sends {ids: []} and toasts 'Refunded 0 orders!'.
remediation: Disable the control until at least one order is selected, show a confirmation naming the count and total, then send; or fix the README.

title: No in-flight guard on refund: double click sends the refund twice
evidence: Handler awaits refund and does not disable the control or carry an idempotency key; selected is not cleared. Traced.
failing_case: Double-click Refund selected with 3 orders selected: two POST /refunds with the same ids are sent; a backend without idempotency refunds twice.
remediation: Disable the control while the request is pending, clear selection on success, and send an idempotency key with each refund request.

title: Refund control is a span: not focusable, no role, not operable by keyboard or announced as a button
evidence: A span without tabindex or role is skipped by Tab and Enter/Space do nothing; only the onclick in app.js:49 handles it. WCAG 2.1.1 (A), 4.1.2 (A). Traced.
failing_case: A keyboard-only user ticks orders with Tab/Space but cannot reach Refund selected at all.
remediation: Use <button type="button" class="refund">.

quote: table { width: 1000px; border-collapse: collapse; background: #fff; border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.1); }
title: Table fixed at 1000px and 3-column stats grid fixed: sideways scroll at 390px and at 200% zoom
evidence: styles.css:13 width:1000px; styles.css:6 repeat(3, 1fr) with no media query anywhere in the file; main has 24px padding. Also the table has border-collapse: collapse so border-radius on it has no effect. Traced.
failing_case: On a 390px phone (or 1360px at 200% zoom, a 680px viewport) the table is 1000px wide and the page scrolls horizontally; the three stat cards squeeze to about 100px each.
remediation: Use width:100% inside an overflow-x:auto wrapper (or reflow rows to cards below 640px) and make .cards a single column under 640px with grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(160px, 1fr)).

title: Focus outline removed with no replacement
evidence: No :focus-visible rule exists in styles.css. Checkboxes keep the default, but search, status, Prev, Next show no focus at all. WCAG 2.4.7 (AA). Traced.
failing_case: Tab to Prev/Next or the search box: nothing changes visually, so a keyboard user cannot tell where they are.
remediation: Delete the rule or replace it with a :focus-visible outline of at least 2px with 3:1 contrast against the background.

title: Performance claim has no measurement and the code path does not support 'instantly'
evidence: No benchmark in the payload. Every keystroke triggers a network request (app.js:45) and renderStats loops all orders; with 10,000 orders the page also gets a 10,000-item JSON per keystroke and no server-side pagination (PAGE_SIZE slices client-side at app.js:28). Inferred, not run.
failing_case: Type in the search box with 10,000 orders: each keystroke downloads the whole list, re-sums it and re-renders, with no loading state.
remediation: Measure it and cite the number, or drop the claim; paginate and debounce server-side.

title: Search text concatenated into the URL without encoding
evidence: query is raw input from #q (app.js:39). No encodeURIComponent; res.ok is also never checked (api.js:7). Traced.
failing_case: Search 'Smith & Sons' sends q=Smith & Sons and the server sees a bare ' Sons' parameter; search 'a&status=refunded#' injects a parameter and truncates the rest of the URL.
remediation: Build the query with URLSearchParams.

title: Discount, tax rate and revenue rules live inside the render function, with float money
evidence: app.js:9-17 applies a 10% gold discount and 8.25% tax inside renderStats. The table (app.js:32) shows raw o.total with no discount or tax, so the table and the REVENUE card use different amounts for the same order. Sums use floating point and toFixed. No test or named function. Traced.
failing_case: A gold customer order of $100 shows as $100 in the table but contributes $97.43 to REVENUE; the operator cannot reconcile the two.
remediation: Move pricing and revenue to one pure, tested function (integer cents, named TAX_RATE and GOLD_DISCOUNT) used by both the stats and the table, or take the figures from the server.

title: Empty result renders $NaN average
evidence: With orders = [] revenue is 0 and 0/0 is NaN; app.js:22 prints '$NaN'. No empty state exists for the table either. Traced.
failing_case: Type a search matching no customers: the stats card reads AVG ORDER $NaN and the table is silently blank.
remediation: Guard orders.length === 0 (show $0.00 / '-') and add an empty-state row saying no orders match and offering to clear filters.

title: Page count rounds down, and Prev/Next/filter changes are not clamped
evidence: Math.floor drops the last partial page (25 orders: 'of 2', 3 pages exist; 5 orders: 'of 0'). app.js:47-48 decrement/increment without bounds; load() (app.js:38-43) does not reset page after a new search or filter. Traced.
failing_case: On page 3 type a search that returns 4 results: the table is empty and the label says 'Page 3 of 0'. Click Prev repeatedly: page goes negative and the slice returns an empty or wrong range.
remediation: Use Math.max(1, Math.ceil(n / PAGE_SIZE)), clamp page in Prev/Next, disable the buttons at the ends, and reset page to 1 in load().

title: Search and status filter have no labels; the first table header is empty
evidence: Only a placeholder names the search box (vanishes on typing); the <select id="status"> at index.html:18 has no label or name at all; the checkbox column <th></th> at index.html:21 is empty. WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2 (A). Traced.
failing_case: A screen reader announces the select as 'combo box, All' with no purpose; once the user types in the search box the only hint of its purpose is gone.
remediation: Add <label for="q">Search customers</label> and <label for="status">Status</label> (visually hidden if needed) and a visually hidden header text for the checkbox column.

title: Toast is not a live region and never closes
evidence: No role="status" or aria-live on #toast; display:none to block (app.js:51) is not announced by screen readers. Nothing ever resets it to hidden, so the previous message stays after a later action. WCAG 4.1.3 (AA). Traced.
failing_case: A screen-reader user clicks Refund and hears nothing; a sighted user sees 'Refunded 3 orders!' stay on screen indefinitely, including while the next refund is pending.
remediation: Add role="status" aria-live="polite" to the toast, set the text rather than toggling display on the container, and clear it after a few seconds or on the next action.

title: Toast pulses forever with no prefers-reduced-motion override
evidence: Infinite scale animation starts automatically and never stops (WCAG 2.2.2 A for content moving over 5s beside other content). No @media (prefers-reduced-motion) block exists. Traced.
failing_case: After a refund, the toast keeps pulsing until page reload; a vestibular-sensitive user cannot turn it off.
remediation: Remove the infinite animation, or play it once and wrap it in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference).
